subject: Stopping the loop: 13 fixes, 0 criteria moved, everything left is yours
body:
Stopping the loop, and telling you why rather than just going quiet.

I re-ran the criterion board after tonight's thirteen fixes. It is UNCHANGED: 13 met, 11 not met,
6 ambiguous, 30 of 46 automated. Exactly where it was before.

That is not a failure and it is worth understanding. The thirteen warrants were real defects -- a
stand-down that still placed orders, an emergency exit that latched permanently on the first
losing trade, a transition matrix built backward in time, an array overrun reachable at startup,
shorts qualified against long gates. But none of them is what a FORGE FINALE criterion measures.
The criteria measure coherence, instrumentation and evidence. The fixes were correctness. Both
matter; they are not the same axis.

So I hit a stop condition I set at the start: three consecutive sessions gaining zero criteria.
Sessions 106 through 110. The loop is ending because it should, not because it broke.

WHAT IS LEFT IS ALL YOURS. Every remaining item is a design decision, not a repair:

1. DECLARE ONE REGIME AUTHORITY, and move the engine.regime assignment to the top of OnTick.
   This is top of the queue and unblocks the most. Right now three classifiers run per decision,
   and "regime 3" means Bearish Reversal to the scorer and NEUTRAL_BULLISH to the gate.

2. THE CALIBRATION RE-RUN IS HELD until you do. I am adopting the coherence pass's reasoning:
   gates come from one classifier, sizing and brackets from two others, so a better number would
   not be evidence of a better system.

3. A case 8 for ClassifyEnhancedRegime and for RegimeHasStructuralConfirmation. Regime 8 is
   currently unreachable as a live regime, and base regime 8 collapses to CONSOLIDATION -- so the
   two states your run thesis is built on do not survive the crossing between taxonomies.

4. The sizing chain and gating ManagePartialProfits, as ONE decision, not two.

5. Rotate the Anthropic API key.

Smaller: a bearish downgrade path to mirror the bullish one, the unwired hysteresis band, and
whether the session TP/SL dimension should become real.

And the one thing the night settled outright: the hit-rate curve is the fair-game curve to within
0.4 of a percentage point. Exit geometry is not what is broken, and no target size clears cost
even with cost set to zero.
